::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Curl of vector triple product.](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3593279/curl-of-vector-triple-product), asked by [huministic](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/677016/huministic) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2020-03-24; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> I want to prove that for given constant vectors **A** and **B**
>
> Curl [ (**R** × **A**) ×**B** ] = **B** × **A**
>
> where **R** = xi + yj + zk
>
> I proved vector triple product using index notation but I don't know how to approach the above problem using index notation.
:::

Using the [BAC-CAB identity](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/BAC-CABIdentity.html):
$$(\mathbf{R} \times \mathbf{A}) \times \mathbf{B}
    = - (\mathbf{A} \cdot \mathbf{B}) \mathbf{R} + (\mathbf{B} \cdot \mathbf{R}) \mathbf{A}$$
Now you can use the [product rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_calculus_identities#Curl_2) for the curl of a scalar times a vector:
$$\nabla((\mathbf{R} \times \mathbf{A}) \times \mathbf{B})
   = - \nabla(\mathbf{A} \cdot \mathbf{B}) \times \mathbf{R}
     - (\mathbf{A} \cdot \mathbf{B}) (\nabla \times \mathbf{R})
     + \nabla(\mathbf{B} \cdot \mathbf{R}) \times \mathbf{A}
     + (\mathbf{B} \cdot \mathbf{R}) (\nabla \times \mathbf{A})$$
Since $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ are constant, $\nabla (\mathbf{A} \cdot \mathbf{B}$ and $\nabla \times \mathbf{A}$ are zero.  Also, $\nabla \times \mathbf{R} = \mathbf{0}$ by calculation.  The only thing left to show is that $\nabla(\mathbf{B} \cdot \mathbf{R}) = \mathbf{B}$, but this is straightforward.

* * *

If you want to use index notation, let $\mathbf{e}_1 = \mathbf{i}$, $\mathbf{e}_2 = \mathbf{j}$, and $\mathbf{e}_3 = \mathbf{k}$.  So we can write $\mathbf{A} = a_i \mathbf{e}_i$ and $\mathbf{B} = b_i \mathbf{e}_i$ (Einstein summation).  Write $x_1 = x$, $x_2 = y$, $x_3 = z$, so $\mathbf{R} = x_i \mathbf{e}_i$.  Let $\epsilon_{ijk}$ be the Levi-Civita tensor, so that
$$\mathbf{A} \times \mathbf{B} = \epsilon_{ijk} a_i b_j \mathbf{e}_k$$
For each $i$, write $\partial_i  = \frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}$.  Notice that $\partial_i x_j = \delta_{ij}$, where $\delta$ is the Kronecker delta tensor.  And if $\mathbf{F} = F_i \mathbf{e}_i$ is a vector field, then
$$\nabla \times \mathbf F = \epsilon_{ijk} \partial_i F_j \mathbf{e}_k$$

Now 
$$\begin{align*}
   \nabla \times ((\mathbf{R} \times \mathbf{A}) \times \mathbf{B})
   &= \epsilon_{ijk} \partial_i ((\mathbf{R} \times \mathbf{A}) \times \mathbf{B})_j \mathbf{e}_k \\
   &= \epsilon_{ijk} \partial_i (\epsilon_{\ell mj} (\mathbf{R} \times \mathbf{A})_\ell b_m)\mathbf{e}_k \\
   &= \epsilon_{ijk} \partial_i (\epsilon_{\ell mj} \epsilon_{rp\ell}x_r a_p  b_m) \mathbf{e}_k\\
   &= \epsilon_{ijk} \epsilon_{\ell mj} \epsilon_{rp\ell} \partial_i x_r a_p  b_m \mathbf{e}_k\\
   &= \epsilon_{ijk} \epsilon_{\ell mj} \epsilon_{rp\ell} \delta_{ir} a_p  b_m \mathbf{e}_k\\
   &= \epsilon_{ijk} \epsilon_{\ell mj} \epsilon_{ip\ell} a_p  b_m \mathbf{e}_k\\
\end{align*}$$
Use the contraction identity on the first and last symbol (they both start with $i$):
$$\epsilon_{ijk}\epsilon_{ip\ell} = \delta_{jp}\delta_{k\ell} - \delta_{j\ell}\delta_{kp}$$
And notice that:
$$\begin{align*}
    \epsilon_{\ell mj}\delta_{jp}\delta_{k\ell} &= \epsilon_{kmp} \\
    \epsilon_{\ell mj}\delta_{j\ell}\delta_{kp} &= \epsilon_{\ell m\ell} = 0
\end{align*}$$
So finally:
$$\nabla \times ((\mathbf{R} \times \mathbf{A}) \times \mathbf{B})
    = \epsilon_{kmp} a_p b_m \mathbf{e}_k
    = \epsilon_{mpk} b_m a_p \mathbf{e}_k
    = \mathbf{B} \times \mathbf{A}$$

I'll point out that the contraction identity for the Levi-Civita tensor is essentially BAC-CAB in index notation.
